seoTitle: Financial Year — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A financial year is the twelve-month period a business reports its accounts for. The twelve-month period a business reports its accounts for.
definition: A financial year is the twelve-month period a business reports its accounts for. In India it runs from 1 April to 31 March, and is written in forms such as FY 2025-26.
bodyHtml:
Why Financial Year matters

Almost every deadline, threshold and invoice series is tied to the financial year. Invoice numbering restarts with it, and turnover thresholds for registration and e-invoicing are measured across it.

How Financial Year works in practice

Plan the year-end sequence in advance: stock count, receivable and payable confirmations, depreciation, accruals, and the invoice series reset on 1 April.

faq.question: Why does India use April to March?
faq.answer: It is the statutory year set by law, and tax rules, returns and thresholds are all aligned to it.

faq.question: Is the assessment year different?
faq.answer: Yes. The assessment year is the year in which the previous financial year's income is assessed to tax.
